description.purpose: The colony, drawn: a timer takes a topology snapshot and a code cell turns it into one view of hives, edges and cells. An app, so it owns no channel and no port -- it produces a picture and a display holds it. The browser owns two things and neither of them is the picture: the drag, and where you are looking. The default picture leaves out the cells that take part in no edge at all -- a live colony collects those, because removing a node disconnects it and never deletes it -- and a button in the legend brings them back. Since 1.0.2 a hive frame is labelled with its LEVEL beside its directory name -- `alex · member` around the person, `alex · assistant` around the agent inside them -- read off the container segment of the path, so nothing new travels on the wire for it.
description.use_when: Somebody should see and rearrange what the colony knows, in a browser, without an operator UI release for every new kind of object. Wire this hive to a display and the view appears there; wire it to two and it appears on both.
description.not_in_scope: It draws nothing the topology snapshot does not hold, and that snapshot arrives on a timer through this hive's OWN lane to the colony's read-only graph endpoint, so the picture is as fresh as that timer. No port and no authentication: an app has no surface, and whatever stands in front of the display stands in front of this. No object vocabulary beyond cells, hives and edges. No interior address: params.ports is empty, so no cell in here is an endpoint -- a caller names the hive and a lane (in_refresh in, view out).
examples: every minute: a topology snapshot becomes one view, and the display it is wired to catches up

a drag lands in the display's own database as an OFFSET beside the layout's own position, and the next view leaves that offset alone -- so the box stays where a hand put it while everything nobody has touched follows the flow
a second display wired to the same hive shows the same picture, and neither of them is named here
